samples.summary: `pointerDriven` gate skips the most common dismissal path (click outside onto the canvas), where Radix *modal* Popovers force focus back onto the toolbar trigger — so issue #882 still reproduces there
samples.evidence: `onFocusIn` bails out unless the last `pointerdown` landed inside the toolbar or a popup (`isPointerDrivenTarget`, lines 80-87). Every slides colour/border picker is a **modal** Popover (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/shape-controls.tsx:219`, `text-element-controls.tsx:118`, `table-controls.tsx:286`, `border-picker.tsx:110`). Radix's `PopoverContentModal` default `onCloseAutoFocus` unconditionally does `context.triggerRef.current?.focus()` (only right-click-outside is exempt), and `useMenuCloseHandlers.onCloseAutoFocus` (`menu-focus.ts:52-57`) only `preventDefault()`s when a swatch was clicked. So: open Fill ▾, dismiss it by clicking the canvas → pointerdown target is outside the toolbar → `pointerDriven = false` → the trigger `<button>` ends up focused and the hook deliberately does nothing. `isEditableTarget` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:882) then keeps eating every shortcut, i.e. the exact bug the change claims to close. Same hole when the user Tabs inside an open picker (Tab clears the flag) and then closes it. Note `menu-focus.ts:26-29` asserts outside-click 'falls through to Radix's default focus-to-trigger, then the natural click target / body keep focus', which is not what modal Popover does.

samples.summary: Release is driven only by `focusin`, so clicking a toolbar button that is already focused never releases focus
samples.evidence: The whole mechanism hangs off `focusin` inside the toolbar. If the button already has focus, a pointer click fires no `focus`/`focusin` event, so nothing is ever scheduled. Reachable path: user Tabs to a toolbar button (Tab sets `pointerDriven = false`, focus stays per design), then clicks that same focused button with the mouse — `pointerDriven` becomes true but no `focusin` arrives, so focus stays on the button and the keydown gate stays engaged. A `pointerup`/`click`-based re-check (or re-checking on `pointerdown` inside the toolbar) would cover it.

samples.summary: `pointerDriven` latches true indefinitely — only a Tab keypress or a pointerdown elsewhere clears it, so a later non-pointer focus arrival in the toolbar is blurred
samples.evidence: `pointerDriven` is set in `onPointerDown` and cleared only on `Tab` (line 104) or by a subsequent pointerdown outside the toolbar/popups. It is never reset after a release. Any programmatic focus into the toolbar that happens after an earlier toolbar click without an intervening Tab or outside pointerdown (e.g. a dialog/panel opened by keyboard whose close restores focus to a toolbar trigger, or an autofocus after a re-render) is treated as 'pointer-driven' and blurred, stealing focus from where the app deliberately put it. Resetting the flag inside the deferred callback would bound its lifetime to the interaction it describes.

samples.summary: `hasOpenPopup`'s `data-state === "open"` check is unreliable for triggers wrapped in a `TooltipTrigger asChild`; only `aria-expanded` actually protects them
samples.evidence: Almost every toolbar trigger is nested as `<TooltipTrigger asChild><DropdownMenuTrigger asChild><button/>` (e.g. `app/slides/toolbar/zoom-control.tsx:55-66`, `app/board/board-toolbar.tsx:198-222`). Radix Slot merges the Tooltip's `data-state` (`closed`/`delayed-open`) into the menu trigger's props, which the menu trigger spreads *after* its own `data-state`, so the rendered attribute is the tooltip's, not `"open"`. Today `aria-expanded="true"` still rescues the guard, so this is latent — but any toolbar popup trigger that signals open state only through `data-state` (a custom controlled popover, a non-Radix menu) would be blurred out from under its own open popup, closing it on the click that opened it.

samples.summary: Hook installs three document-level capture listeners even on the mobile path, where no `data-canvas-toolbar` element is ever rendered
samples.evidence: `useCanvasFocusRelease()` is called before the `if (isMobile) return <MobileSlidesToolbar …>` early return (lines 70 and 92-107) and `MobileSlidesToolbar` never sets `data-canvas-toolbar`, so the pointerdown/keydown/focusin capture listeners run for every event in the app with no possible effect. Harmless but pure overhead; gating on `!isMobile` (or passing an enabled flag) would avoid it.

verdict.reason: The described code is present and unguarded. `onFocusIn` bails unless `pointerDriven` (toolbar-focus-release.ts:107-108), and `pointerDriven` is set only when the last pointerdown landed inside `[data-canvas-toolbar]` or a popup (lines 81-87, 99-101); `Tab` also clears it (103-105). The slides colour/border pickers are all `modal` Popovers (shape-controls.tsx:219, text-element-controls.tsx:118, table-controls.tsx:286, border-picker.tsx:110) on @radix-ui/react-popover ^1.1.7 (package.json:42), whose modal content's default onCloseAutoFocus refocuses the trigger for anything but a right-click-outside. The repo's own handler only intervenes for swatch clicks (menu-focus.ts:52-57 returns early when `swatchClickedRef` is false), the ui/popover.tsx wrapper adds no default onCloseAutoFocus, and onFillOpenChange (shape-controls.tsx:156-165) only flushes a gradient draft. These triggers carry no `data-text-edit-keepalive`, so they are not the documented exempt case. Result: dismissing a picker by clicking the canvas leaves the trigger `<button>` focused, and `isEditableTarget` (keyboard.ts:871-890, BUTTON at 882) keeps swallowing every shortcut gated on `!isEditableTarget(e.target)` (e.g. keyboard.ts:131, 218, 505, 549) — the exact #882 behavior. No test in toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx exercises outside-click dismissal or a modal Popover. Real logic gap in a core flow: major/blocking under the correctness rubric.
